claim: Token-prefix validity does not imply state validity. On a hybrid-architecture model (GLM's interleaved attention layers), an externally transferred KV cache can report a COMPLETE hit while the resumed model is internally inconsistent: the cache boundary proves which tokens were seen, not that every layer's state matches the checkpoint, kernels, and schedule that produced it. Verified against the arXiv abstract this ask: the quoted sentence is the abstract's first line; the cure is strict-prefix lookup (recover only up to the longest verified token prefix, never the nominal complete-hit boundary), fixed per-rank kernel configurations (determinism pinning; the mismatch that credited one fewer token was unpinned kernels, not missing data), and a CPU-reload tier that cuts TTFT 46-64% at 1.9-7.0% total-time cost, with agreement going 34/36 to 36/36 after alignment on the RedHatAI GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 checkpoint under four-way TP. One-line law to mint: NO CACHE RESUME WITHOUT A VERIFIED-PREFIX RECEIPT, AND NO HIT KPI THAT COUNTS UNRECEIPTED HITS. Paper verified live at https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15030; overlap re-verified: 0 catalog rows (grep -c on catalog/catalog.jsonl), 0 ARXIV_REGISTER entries (grep -c on memory/runs/corpus_gap_research/ARXIV_REGISTER.json), exactly 1 raw-census mention in watch/inbox/frontier_olm_2026-10-03/sweep/_raw/q1_candidates.json; the find is lane item 2 at watch/inbox/frontier_olm_2026-10-04/sweep/kv-cache-and-context-engineering-arxiv.md:35.
